sources.scope: Public explanation of IPS sky-map projections; useful data-display context, not independent named-lab scope.
Explicit Solar Group at A&A near-real-time solar-wind reconstruction/forecast project, using IPS observations supplied by ISEE Nagoya.

candidateProjectSummaryZh: 该无日期技术介绍描述 A&A Solar Group 的太阳风重建项目：利用名古屋大学 ISEE 提供的行星际闪烁（IPS）资料，重建太阳风密度与速度结构，研究近地太阳风条件及扰动到达。页面列出运动学模型、迭代最小二乘拟合、日球层层析及航天器观测数据比较；其与 baseline Space Weather Laboratory 的现行实体映射仍待官方目录核实。
candidateResearchQuestionsZh: 如何由沿视线积分的 IPS 观测重建太阳风密度与速度结构？
如何以太阳风重建预测近地条件和扰动到达？
candidateTopicsZh: 近地空间天气与太阳风扰动
共转及随时间变化的太阳风模型
candidateMethodsZh: 与航天器观测数据比较
optionalDisplayMethodsZh: 鱼眼（等距方位）与 Hammer-Aitoff 天空图投影，仅属数据展示

evidence.quote: an ongoing project in the Solar Group at A&A
evidence.scope: Named project/group scope only; does not itself name the baseline Space Weather Laboratory.

evidence.quote: Our goal is to forecast solar wind conditions in the near-Earth environment, and predict the arrival of solar wind structures at Earth.
evidence.scope: Project goal stated at an unknown content date; not a claim of present-day operational forecast delivery.

evidence.quote: The reconstructions of the solar wind are based on a kinematic model of the solar wind.
The reconstruction of the solar wind is based on an iterative least-squares algorithm.
We use a tomographic technique to disentangle this line-of-sight smearing.
evidence.scope: Project's line-of-sight reconstruction, explicitly called heliospheric tomography later.

evidence.quote: We use observations from spacecraft instruments to provide corraborative space weather data.
evidence.scope: Use/comparison of spacecraft data, not ownership or operation of spacecraft.

evidence.quote: We show forecast results from two different models: a corotating (or time-independent ) model and a time-dependent model.
evidence.scope: Two modelling choices described by this project.
Sky-map display/projection method only; not an additional laboratory experiment.

No foreign sites, instrument links, examples, animations, publications or cited papers were followed.
